source.author: hor
source.text: ut scriptor si peccat idem librarius usque, quamvis est monitus, venia caret, et citharoedus ridetur, chorda qui semper oberrat eadem, sic mihi, qui multum cessat, fit Choerilus ille, quem bis terve bonum cum risu miror; et idem indignor, quandoque bonus dormitat Homerus; verum operi longo fas est obrepere somnum.
source.text_original: ut scriptor si peccat idem librarius usque,  / quamvis est monitus, venia caret, et citharoedus  / ridetur, chorda qui semper oberrat eadem,  / sic mihi, qui multum cessat, fit Choerilus ille,  / quem bis terve bonum cum risu miror; et idem  / indignor, quandoque bonus dormitat Homerus;  / verum operi longo fas est obrepere somnum.
source.text_english: as when a copyist, if he makes the same mistake over and over, though he has been warned, is without excuse, and the cithara-player is laughed at who is always blundering on the same string, so for me the man who is very often lazy turns into that Choerilus, whom, though he is good two or three times, I wonder at with a laugh; and likewise I am indignant whenever good Homer nods off; yet in a long work sleep is allowed to creep in.

reuse.author: hier
reuse.text: quodsi quis ludas zelotes opposuerit nobis errores eius, audiat libere: interdum magnus dormitat Homerus, uerum operi longo fas est ignoscere somnum.
reuse.text_original: quodsi quis ludas zelotes opposuerit nobis errores eius, audiat libere: interdum magnus dormitat Homerus, uerum operi longo fas est ignoscere somnum.
reuse.text_english: But if anyone should set against us the mistakes of that zealot Judas, let him hear freely: even great Homer sometimes nods, yet in a long work it is right to pardon sleep.
